steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Are you ready?
Yes.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: On my cue. Three, two...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: One!
On the clearing beside the old town, the ethereal woman wields the Apostle's power in tandem with your Potestas, steadily raising a high tower.
Foundation, timber, and stone weave and fuse at her command as if enchanted, drawing the peak skyward, floor upon rising floor.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: A day ago, I never would've imagined using Mania to build something like this in my lifetime. Let's finish this in one push.
She turns back to you, offering a smile and a nod.
As you wish.
One Day Ago

steps.speaker: Supervision Center
steps.content: WARNING: Furnace temperature exceeding safe levels.

steps.speaker: Supervision Center
steps.content: WARNING: Furnace temperature exceeding safe levels.

Evening settles in. During the shift change, the temperature in the furnace area adjacent to the cafeteria lounge suddenly soars. The mercury column in the thermometer edges slowly higher, still short of the critical threshold.
Beneath the monitor's stuttering red warning, small clusters of sparks flicker and dance, hopping as they weave and meld. An orange-red feather drifts down to the table and burns with a sharp hiss.
In a corner nearby, something small whimpers softly.
Chirp...?

steps.speaker: Staff A
steps.content: So where you headed this year?

steps.speaker: Staff B
steps.content: Ah, last year was my folks' place, so this year it's the in-laws.

steps.speaker: Staff A
steps.content: That's nice... I can't wait to get home myself...

steps.speaker: Staff B
steps.content: Yeah, tell me about it... Hey, uh, is it just me, or is it getting really hot by the furnace?
The two staff members chat as they step out of the cafeteria, only to notice the abnormal heat radiating from the furnace area.
Waves of heat push through the gap in the door. Something is definitely wrong. The staff members trade a look and nod. One of them carefully wraps a hand around the handle.

steps.speaker: Staff A
steps.content: Alright, you ready? I got you.

steps.speaker: Staff B
steps.content: Yeah, ready...
The staff member counts down in silence for a few seconds, then hauls open the door to the furnace area.
Cheeeeeep!
A scorching gust howls past them, and both workers duck on instinct, throwing their hands up to shield themselves.
Even as they drop low, they glimpse an orange-red ball of light, radiating intense heat, stumbling past their feet at breakneck speed.

steps.speaker: Staff A
steps.content: What is that...?

steps.speaker: Staff B
steps.content: Did that fire just... become something alive?

steps.speaker: Noisy Voices
steps.content: Wait, where'd it go?!

steps.speaker: Noisy Voices
steps.content: Is it somewhere near you?!

steps.speaker: Noisy Voices
steps.content: Behind you! Look behind you!!

steps.speaker: Noisy Voices
steps.content: Careful, don't step on it—whoa!
Coming back from fieldwork, you find yourself constantly rubbing your face against the winter chill, longing for nothing more than to slip back into the Bureau and warm your bones.
But the Bureau greets you with unexpected warmth today, and something else besides... a strange liveliness.

steps.speaker: Yanyan
steps.content: OwO! Over here, over here! It's heading your way. Get the board ready!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Hehe, you little troublemaker! Just wait till the great OwO gets her hands on—whoa, whoa, whoa!
Whack!

steps.speaker: Yanyan
steps.content: Ah! Chief!! Look out!!!
The voices find you just as you are slipping off your coat and making your way toward the commotion, curious to discover what all the fuss is about.
The shout jerks your gaze forward on instinct, but the moment you raise your head, something warm, soft, and fluffy slams right into your face.
Cheep...
Slowly, you reach up and pinch whatever has latched onto your face, clinging to your hair for dear life, and carefully peel it away. You bring it closer to inspect—
A small bird, vivid orange-red and wreathed in shimmering heat, rests in your palm. Something has clearly agitated it; the tips of its feathers are visibly singed.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Yao?
It looks nothing like what you expect, and its power reads as faint, yet your shackles leave no doubt: this little bird's power source traces back to Yao.

steps.speaker: Yanyan
steps.content: Wait, that's Yao?!

steps.speaker: Yanyan
steps.content: Chief
Yanyan steps out from the clutter and gently scoops the little bird into her hands, staring at it with disbelief. Perhaps sensing that the chase is over, the bird makes no attempt to flee.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The power signature matches hers. I'm thinking... maybe a clone? She might've made it by accident when her power spiked again.

steps.speaker: Yanyan
steps.content: Really? Is she okay, though? We just got some new books in from Eastia, and I read that super powerful people can lose control when they're trying to break past their limits. What if something happened to her?!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Don't worry. The energy feels gentle. If something was really wrong with Yao, it wouldn't be this calm. That's probably why you couldn't tell it was connected to her.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'll go check on her myself. You two...
You retrieve the little creature from Yanyan and take in the chaos that surrounds you: spell-scorched ashes and black smoke, wooden boards from hurried traps, plastic bags strewn about...

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: I-it was their idea! They said there was a little spirit running around, so I just... I was just helping!
OwO catches your look and quickly ducks behind the two staff members, pouting with an expression that screams innocence, as if none of this mess could possibly be her fault.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It's fine. You two go take a break. Let the adults handle the rest.
The two staff members nod eagerly. One ushers Yanyan and OwO clear of the mess; the other goes in search of a broom, muttering under their breath about how swamped they are.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Alright, little guy. Let's go figure out where you came from.
The WhiteSands had seen numerous disturbances of late, but Yao put down every last one. WhiteSands has remained relatively peaceful ever since.
Around the New Year, a letter arrived for you, marked with a flame feather and bearing words that she would return to the Bureau in a few days to visit.
Perhaps the effort of suppressing the Apostles had taken too much out of her. Since Yao came back, she has kept mostly to her room, sleeping, and only stirring for meals.

steps.speaker: Fledgling?
steps.content: Chirp! Cheeeep!
As though it senses something, the fledgling in your palm stirs with sudden excitement, its wings beating frantically.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Yeah, yeah. Hang on. We're almost there.
Yao's room feels warmer than any other. Even in the dead of winter, the door handle holds its warmth against your palm.

You push the door open. There she lies, curled up in bed and fast asleep, just as you expect. Soft blankets wrap her from head to toe, letting only her long, lovely hair spill free—flowing like a cascade of tail feathers.

steps.speaker: Fledgling?
steps.content: Chirp, chirp, chirp! Chirp, chirp!

You set the fledgling down beside Yao's pillow. It nuzzles into her hair with obvious delight. You had thought it might revert to a single feather or melt back into raw energy, sinking into Yao once more, but the little bird shows no such intention.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: Chief...?

The bird latches onto a strand of hair and gives a sharp tug, startling the sleeper into consciousness. A bout of muffled grumbling rises from under the blankets before Yao finally surfaces, eyes still half-closed.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: Is something the matter? And this little one... where did it come from?
Yao scoops up the little bird from beside her pillow and gazes into its beady eyes for a long moment. It doesn't take her long to realize that this creature has sprung from her own excess power.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: You came all this way just to bring it back yourself... I take it this little one has been causing mischief?
You chuckle under your breath and drop into a crouch by the bed. One quick poke at the creature in Yao's palm, then you pull out your terminal to check.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Two staff members spotted it hanging around the furnace area. They tried to catch it, and it just bolted. Left sparks everywhere it went.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Nothing too bad, honestly. Scared a few people, a couple dropped plates, some files went flying... Oh, and it set a few cardboard boxes on fire.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But I'm more curious about how it even got there in the first place...
Once she has heard your account, Yao presses her lips into a thin line and gives the little bird a poke. Unrepentant as ever, it simply stares back. She speaks, her voice low.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: ...I've felt safe here at the Bureau. And with you nearby so often lately, my power has been returning faster than I expected. I think... that may be why this little one appeared.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: I should reabsorb it at once. Before it stirs up any more trouble.

A slow stream of golden-red light seeps from Yao's palm, wrapping around the little bird. Yet even after a long moment passes, the fledgling refuses to merge back into her. If anything, it only grows larger.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Did it just get fatter?

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: Fluffed up.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Right. Fluffed up.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: Still... that it refuses to return to me is strange.
Yao contemplates this for a moment, then suddenly asks.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: Chief, where did you find it?
You lead Yao to the furnace area. The fledgling clearly approves of this place as it bounces back and forth in her palm, fluttering with visible excitement.
Yao lets her gaze drift over the furnace area, then it finally lands on the little cafeteria just beyond.
It happens to be the midnight shift change. The cafeteria has laid out late-night snacks, and staff clusters together, eating and talking. The talk, as ever, revolves around the coming spring break.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: I think I understand now...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: It came from me, yes... but what gave it shape was something else entirely.
Yao nods toward the staff members chattering away in the cafeteria, the ghost of a smile pulling at the corners of her mouth.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: In the beginning, the Sun Crow took form because of what people held in their hearts... their faith, their hopes, their wishes.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: This little one's power may have come from the feather I sent you... but the reason it lives...

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: ...is because of the longing and wishes they carry as they speak.
Yao runs her fingers gently over the fledgling's feathers. A pleasant shiver ripples from the crown of its head all the way to the end of its tail.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: I don't think a simple recall will be enough to bring it back into my core power... Not as it is now.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So what do we do?
You prod the fledgling's belly softly, then study it once more as you withdraw your hand.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Whatever's in those wishes... it's got some serious fuel behind it. Pretty sure it got bigger since earlier, ahem, I mean, fluffier.
Yao cocks her head, catching the drift of conversation, then answers with a thoughtful air.

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: In ancient times, when deities heard the prayers of their people...

steps.speaker: Yao
steps.content: They surely would want to answer them themselves.
